7
What is the definition of linear momentum?
A
force per unit time
B
product of force and time
C
product of velocity and mass
D
velocity per unit mass

hints: Notice the wording asks for linear momentum itself, not the change in momentum during a collision.
Recall how mass in $\text{kg}$ and velocity in $\text{m s}^{-1}$ combine to give momentum in $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$.
Compare $mv$ with $Ft$: one defines the momentum an object has, the other defines the impulse that changes it.
walkthrough: Identify what is asked: the defining quantities for linear momentum of a moving object.
State the governing definition: linear momentum $p$ is a vector defined by $p = mv$.
Check the meaning: larger mass at the same velocity, or larger velocity at the same mass, gives larger momentum with unit $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$.
Compare with the distractors: $Ft$ is impulse equal to change in momentum $\Delta p$, while $F/t$ and $v/m$ do not match the definition or units.
Therefore the product of velocity and mass matches $p = mv$. This is option C

A.explanation: Force per unit time is $F/t$, which has units of $\text{N s}^{-1}$ and is not momentum.

B.explanation: Product of force and time is $Ft$, which is impulse or change in momentum, not momentum itself.

C.explanation: Linear momentum is defined by $p = mv$, the product of mass and velocity.

D.explanation: Velocity per unit mass is $v/m$, which does not give the unit $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$ of momentum.
